biomes.name: ria valley
biomes.notes: The Great Ria River Valley: broad fertile alluvial and terraced valley sloping continuously from the Eastern Highland Lake (+1,460 m) and Tharn foothills westward to the Ring/NW Ocean. Once settled by the Ancients; hosts a rich hybrid ecology of Earthlike gallery forests, terraced orchards, and alien symbiotic flora.

biomes.name: arachnoid canyons
biomes.notes: Venusian Volcano-Tectonic Arachnoid Network & The Web-Cleaver Gorge: concentric ring-dike cauldrons and radial extensional fracture canyons straddling northern, eastern, and SW Korona and the southern Ria Valley rim. Cleaved by a dramatic 1,200–1,850 m-deep sinuous canyon carrying the Highland Lake river through northern Korona down into the Ria River.

biomes.name: tharn uplands
biomes.notes: NE Tharn Uplands & Outer Rim: high, cold-dry windswept alpine and hypobaric outer-rim plateau (+5,800 to +9,800 m) inspired by Chris Wayan's Tharn, where high-elevation freeze-thaw aridity meets the airless outer crater rim.

biomes.name: ne outer wall
biomes.notes: NE Outer Wall — The Glass-Skarn Bastion (101,372 km²): a structurally unique impact-crater rim bastion wedged between the Northern Korona volcano-tectonic dome, the Arachnoid radial dike swarm, Spider Lake, and the Outland Gate fault. Features 3 geothermally heated Boxwork Dike-Cauldrons (+2,670 to +2,950 m warm hydrothermal tarns), pistachio-green epidote and wine-red grossular garnet contact-metamorphic skarn badlands, and black pseudotachylite fault mirrors.

biomes.name: spider lake
biomes.notes: Spider Lake Highland Silk-Forest Basin (72,928 km²): centered on the +1,460.0 m hydrothermal highland lake (1.20 atm, 0.26 atm O₂, Cfa/Cfb). Sublacustrine warm seeps fuel year-round "lake-smoke" midge clouds that sustain permanent 200,000-strong colonies of eusocial spiders (Arachneapolita sericifera) and live rotational silk-weir arachniculture (see biomes/spiderlake/PLAN.md).

biomes.name: neo-ozarks
biomes.notes: Neo-Ozarks Dissected Carbonate & Porphyry Plateau (56,684 km²): an ancient epeirogenic tableland of flat-lying cherty dolomite and limestone (+1,260 to +1,680 m) deeply dissected by spring-fed hollows and first-magnitude karst caverns. Famous for its 5 strike-aligned exposed veins and knobs of purple-red rhyolite porphyry (+180 to +320 m ridges) where rivers carve boulder-choked canyon shut-ins.

settlements.name: The Gate
settlements.notes: The one way into the Outlands: the Outland Gate's Narrows (1,423 m, 1.34 atm), held by the Tierhounds' long wall from wall foot to wall foot (1431,326 to 1446,326) and their toll fort and water gate on the river, with the trickster's shrine; the god's road (Sleeping City to Trickster's House) runs through it. Moved from the old 7.7 km pass (1408,414), which keeps a cairn and a shrine. biomes/outlandgate/PLAN.md section 5, biomes/outlands/PLAN.md; the owner, 2026-10-26 and 2026-11-09.

tubes.name: Neo-Ozarks Dolomite Karst & Porphyry-Vein Cavern System

caverns.name: Cathedral of the Red Porphyry Vein
caverns.notes: Vast phreatic dissolution hall in the Neo-Ozarks where groundwater dissolved cherty Gasconade-type dolomite along an impermeable dike wall of polished purple-red rhyolite porphyry.

caverns.name: Onyx Pillar & Chert-Bridge Labyrinth
caverns.notes: Multi-level dolomite and limestone cavern famous for 20-meter banded cave-onyx columns, suspended chert-breccia bridges, and copper-iron porphyry mineral veins.

caverns.name: The Shut-In Big Spring Resurgence
caverns.notes: First-magnitude karst spring cavern discharging emerald calcium-magnesium water through a breached porphyry shut-in gorge into the Neo-Ozark Porphyry Fork.

tubes.name: Epidote Cave

caverns.name: The Portal
caverns.notes: The cave's outer mouth at the head of the Portal Valley, 5,900 m (0.77 atm, EF), under the portal's ice.

caverns.name: The Marble Hall
caverns.notes: The upper level's great chamber under the crest (ground 11.8-12.1 km, about 6.2 km of rock overhead): white skarn marble dissolved from below, gypsum crust and cupolas, dry since the old water table fell.

caverns.name: The Inner Mouth
caverns.notes: The lower level's outlet on the Epidote-Steam Tarn's north shore, about 2,700 m, 30 m over the water: warm, CO2- and H2S-charged water and steam, sinter and mats round it.

tubes.notes: A hypogene cave (water from below, as Carlsbad and Lechuguilla) dissolved in the marble bands of the skarn along the Outland Gate fault (NNW-SSE), the only way into the sealed Epidote-Steam Tarn. The way in: the Portal Valley (1330,295 to 1331,302, floor 5,530-5,900 m, 14 km), then the cave. Floors (depth_m does not describe them): the upper level holds 5.6-5.9 km from the portal (5,900 m) to under the cauldron's rim (y 333); the lower level then falls about 2.9 km to the inner mouth (~2,700 m) in its last 6-8 km. Rock overhead peaks at about 6.4 km under the crest (1336,329, 12.1 km). No point of the walk stands over 5.9 km. A record only: nothing is carved. biomes/neouterwall/PLAN.md section 2a; the owner, 2026-11-09.
